# Exporting Web Services (Delphi)

> [!Note]
> This demo is available in your FlexCel installation at ***&lt;FlexCel Install Folder>*\\Demo\\Delphi\\Modules\\20\.Reports\\27\.Exporting Web Services** and also at [https:&#8203;//&#8203;github.&#8203;com/&#8203;tmssoftware/&#8203;TMS-&#8203;FlexCel.&#8203;VCL-&#8203;demos/&#8203;tree/&#8203;master/&#8203;Delphi/&#8203;Modules/&#8203;20.&#8203;Reports/&#8203;27.&#8203;Exporting Web Services](https://github\.com/tmssoftware/TMS\-FlexCel\.VCL\-demos/tree/master/Delphi/Modules/20\.Reports/27\.Exporting%20Web%20Services)


## Overview


A demo that accesses the NOAA Meteorological web service and returns an
Excel file with the forecast. Just in case you do not have an Internet
connection available, some sample data is included to work offline too.

## Concepts

How to export the data on a Web Service to Excel or PDF.

### UMainForm.pas

<pre class="shiki shiki-themes light-plus dark-plus" style="background-color:#FFFFFF;--shiki-dark-bg:#1E1E1E;color:#000000;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#0000FF;--shiki-dark:#569CD6">unit</span><span style="color:#000000;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4"> UMainForm;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955">{*This program is inspired on the progam by Mikhail Arkhipov</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"> * at http://blogs.msdn.com/mikhailarkhipov/archive/2004/08/12/213963.aspx</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"> * Thanks!</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"> */</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955">/* UPDATE: This was patched with the info on</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"> * http://weblogs.asp.net/jan/archive/2004/01/28/63771.aspx</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"> * to make it work.</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"> *</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"> * Thanks again...</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"> *</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"> * UPDATE 2!</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"> * The NOAA broke the service again, and it has not fixed it for more than a year.</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"> * I give up. We will use http://www.webservicex.net/WeatherForecast.asmx instead.</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"> * The code for NOAA is still there on the SetupNOAA method, just not used so you can see it (and try it if it ever starts working again)</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"> *</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"> * UPDATE 3!</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"> * Now WebserviceX is not working, going back to NOAA. As you can see, it isn't very trustable that a webservice will be there in the</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"> * future, so this demo might not work in online mode when you try it. But you can always look at in in offline mode.</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#008000;--shiki-dark:#6A9955"> * *}</span></span>
